hints.title: Descending Greedy Choice
hints.text: Sort maximumHeight in descending order. To maximize total sum, greedily assign each tower the largest possible strictly decreasing positive integer.

hints.title: Upper Bound Relaxation
hints.text: For each tower with maximum limit h, assign height min(curr - 1, h), where curr is the height assigned to the previously placed tower.

hints.title: Infeasibility Check
hints.text: If at any point the assigned height is less than or equal to 0, it is impossible to give every tower a unique positive integer height. Return -1.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maximumTotalSum(self, maximumHeight: list[int]) -> int:
        maximumHeight.sort(reverse=True)
        curr = float('inf')
        total = 0
        for h in maximumHeight:
            assigned = min(curr - 1, h)
            if assigned <= 0:
                return -1
            total += assigned
            curr = assigned
        return total
```

complexity.notes: Sorting takes O(n log n). The greedy assignment runs in O(n) time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Iterative decrement search or set insertion takes O(n^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place sorting uses O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identifies greedy descending assignment and detects impossible configurations early.
